Three steps to start building with ZAK — components ship as pure CSS hooks with an optional vanilla-JS runtime. No Tailwind, no framework, no global reset.

    Install the packagenpm install zakuikit
  2. 2
    Import the stylesheetimport 'zakuikit/css';

    Use a component<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled">Save</button>
Prefer a CDN? Two tags from jsDelivr work identically — see the Installation guide.

Get StartedZero dependencies

Introduction

ZAKUIKit is an enterprise design system written in pure CSS and vanilla ES6 modules — 176 components across 15 categories, native light/dark theming, and a single stylesheet + script that drop into any page.

Architecture

Everything lives in a cascade layer order — @layer zak.tokens, zak.base, zak.components — so your own unlayered CSS always wins without !important. Colour, spacing, radius and elevation come from the token layer, which re-maps for [data-theme="dark"], so every component inherits the active theme automatically.

There is no runtime framework, no hydration and no build requirement on the consuming side — this entire documentation page is one static HTML file driven by `zak.js`.
jsDelivrnpm

Installation

One build feeds every channel — drop-in CDN tags, two local files, or modular npm imports. All consume the same `zak.css` + `zak.js`.

Option 1 — CDN Recommended

Two tags plus the inline theme boot in <head> — jsDelivr serves the package straight to the browser:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/zakuikit@latest/dist/zak.min.css">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/zakuikit@latest/dist/zak.min.js" defer></script>
Production pages should pin a version (zakuikit@2.2.0) and add an integrity hash. Always keep the inline theme-boot script in <head> so the first paint is flash-free.

Option 2 — Local files

Copy zak.css and zak.js from package/dist/ beside your assets and serve them from your origin — no CDN, no build step:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/zak.css">
<script src="/assets/zak.js" defer></script>

Option 3 — npm

Run npm install zakuikit, then import the stylesheet and the named controller exports:

// Terminal
npm install zakuikit

// Entry file — styles first, then behaviour.
import 'zakuikit/css';

// Or take the named controller exports:
import { ZakModal, ZakTabs, toast } from 'zakuikit';
toast('Saved', 'success', { desc: '3 records updated.' });
Theming

Theming

Light and dark are driven by CSS custom properties behind [data-theme], with a zero-FOUC inline boot.

Theme boot

Drop this in <head> — it reads localStorage, falls back to the system prefers-color-scheme, and sets data-theme before the first paint:

<script>
(function () {
  var t = localStorage.getItem('zak-theme');
  if (t !== 'light' && t !== 'dark')
    t = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches ? 'dark' : 'light';
  document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', t);
})();
</script>

<!-- The toggle just flips the attribute; zak.js persists it. -->
<button data-theme-toggle aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Toggle theme">Light / Dark</button>

  --zak-text-primary: #0f172a;

  --zak-text-primary: #f1f5fb;
}

Usage

Contrast: primary text pairs are tuned to pass WCAG AA (4.5:1) in both themes.
Status colors ship as triples — --zak-{tone}, --zak-{tone}-text, --zak-{tone}-subtle — for accent, text and surface use.
Chart colors --zak-chart-1…7 are theme-aware and ordered for maximum adjacent contrast.

Fluid text

zak-fluid-* interpolates between breakpoints with clamp() — no media queries needed.

This paragraph grows smoothly from 1.25rem to 1.75rem as the viewport widens.

<p class="zak-fluid-xl">Fluid heading — scales between breakpoints.</p>
/* The recipe behind every zak-fluid-* class */
.zak-fluid-xl { font-size: clamp(1.25rem, 1.1rem + 0.7vw, 1.75rem); }

Usage

Numerals in metrics use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so values do not jitter while updating.

Five breakpoints, a fluid layout grid and container-query recipes. Layout primitives respond to their own container when components must be reusable across contexts.

Container queries

This card switches from stacked to horizontal layout once its container — not the viewport — passes 480px. Resize the window to feel it.

<!-- Fluid grid: tracks wrap below the minimum width -->
<div class="zak-lgrid" style="--zak-lgrid-min: 160px">
  <div class="zak-box">Track 1</div>
  <div class="zak-box">Track 2</div>
  <div class="zak-box">Track 3</div>
</div>

<!-- Opt a zone into container queries -->
<div class="zone" style="container-type: inline-size">…</div>

<!-- Respond to the component's own width, not the viewport -->
<style>@container (min-width: 480px) { .zone .card { grid-template-columns: 96px 1fr; } }</style>
@media (max-width: 768px)  { /* tablet: collapse to 1 column */ }
@media (min-width: 1024px) { /* desktop: full chrome */ }
@media (min-width: 1280px) { /* wide: 3–4 column dashboards */ }

Responsive display

zak-hidden-up-* hides from a breakpoint and wider; zak-hidden-down-* hides below it. Resize the window to watch the chips swap.

Hidden ≥ 768px (md) Only ≥ 768px (md) Hidden ≥ 1024px (lg) Always visible

// Toggle loading state without layout shift
const btn = document.querySelector('.zak-btn');
btn.classList.add('is-loading');
btn.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
btn.addEventListener('animationend', () => {
  btn.classList.remove('is-loading');
  btn.removeAttribute('aria-busy');
}, { once: true });

// Controller usage
import { ZakButton } from 'zakuikit';
const button = new ZakButton('#save-btn');
await button.withLoading(saveData);

Link

Navigational actions inside copy — collapses to inline text.

No project yet. to get started.

Five heights from 28 to 52 px; density is a class, never an inline style.

With icons

Icons are decorative by default; the label carries the accessible name.

</button>

Full width

Block buttons stretch to their container — form panels and mobile sheets.

Disabled

Blocks pointer events and dims the control; keep it focusable with aria-disabled instead.

<!-- Hard disable -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled" type="button" disabled>Disabled</button>

<!-- Stays in the tab order; guard the click handler yourself -->

Loading

Spinner swaps in without changing the button width, so the layout never jumps.

<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled is-loading" type="button" aria-busy="true">
  <span class="zak-btn__spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span>Saving…</span>
</button>

Usage

Hierarchy rule of thumb: one filled per view region, outlined for adjacent actions, text for low-emphasis toolbar actions.
The link variant collapses to inline text and is intended for navigational actions inside copy.

disabledbooleanfalseBlocks interaction; opacity 0.48, pointer-events none.
loadingbooleanfalseShows an inline spinner and sets aria-busy.
typeenumbuttonNative button type: button · submit · reset.

  <span>Click to toggle loading</span>

button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  button.classList.add('is-loading');
  button.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');
  try {
    await save();
  } finally {
    button.classList.remove('is-loading');
    button.removeAttribute('aria-busy');
  }
});

// Controller usage
import { ZakButton } from 'zakuikit';
const button = new ZakButton('#save-btn');
await button.withLoading(saveData);

ButtonsStablev1.1

Button Toggle

A button that stays pressed. Use `aria-pressed` as the source of truth; the `is-active` class mirrors it visually. `data-zak-toggleable` flips both on click.

Demo

Pressed-state toggle button for toolbars and filters.

<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-toggle-btn"
  data-zak-toggleable
></button>
<!-- Off: aria-pressed="false" -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-toggle-btn" aria-pressed="false" data-zak-toggleable type="button"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Favorite</button>

<!-- On: is-active mirrors aria-pressed="true" -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-toggle-btn is-active" aria-pressed="true" data-zak-toggleable type="button"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Watching</button>

<!-- data-zak-toggleable auto-toggles the class + aria on click -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-toggle-btn" aria-pressed="false" data-zak-toggleable type="button"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Notify me</button>

Usage

Formerly documented under Forms as “Toggle”; the .zak-toggle-btn class is unchanged.

Forms

Form scaffolding: a `.zak-form` stack, an auto-fit `.zak-form-grid`, inline rows and fieldset grouping for sections inside long forms.

Form scaffolding, grids, rows and fieldsets.

Account

<form class="zak-form" onsubmit="return false">
  <fieldset class="zak-fieldset">
    <legend class="zak-fieldset__legend">Account</legend>
    <div class="zak-form-grid">
      <div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
        <label class="zak-label" for="f-given">Given name</label>
        <input class="zak-input" id="f-given" placeholder="Ada"/>
      </div>
      <div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
        <label class="zak-label" for="f-family">Family name</label>
        <input class="zak-input" id="f-family" placeholder="Lovelace"/>
      </div>
    </div>
  </fieldset>
  <div class="zak-form-row zak-form-row--inline">
    <label class="zak-label" for="f-mail">Email</label>
    <input class="zak-input" id="f-mail" type="email" placeholder="ada@example.dev"/>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-flex" style="justify-content:flex-end">
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--text" type="reset">Reset</button>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled" type="submit">Create account</button>

</form>

The canonical field wrapper: label, control, hint and message slots wired together with `aria-describedby` so validation is announced, not just colored. Variant modifiers restyle the control surface: filled, outlined, underline and ghost.

<input class="zak-input zak-input--ghost" placeholder="Ghost" type="text"/>

Field variants

The variant class goes on the .zak-field wrapper; the control inherits the surface.

<div class="zak-field zak-field--filled">

  <input class="zak-input" id="a" type="text"/>
</div>

  <input class="zak-input" id="c" type="text"/>
</div>

Read-only and disabled

Read-only stays in the tab order and is copyable; disabled leaves it entirely.

<!-- Read-only: selectable, still focusable -->
<input class="zak-input" id="ro" value="https://api.zakui.dev/v1" readonly type="text"/>

<!-- Disabled: out of the tab order -->
<input class="zak-input" id="dis" value="Locked by plan" disabled type="text"/>

With a leading icon

.zak-input-wrap positions the icon inside the field surface — no extra padding classes.

<div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
  <label class="zak-label" for="q">Search</label>
  <div class="zak-input-wrap">
    <svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg>
    <input class="zak-input" id="q" type="search" placeholder="Search deployments…"/>
  </div>
</div>

Input Group

A Form Field with segments: the `.zak-input-group` container draws the single field surface (border, radius, focus ring) and every addon, icon or button inside is borderless, so the row reads as one control. Text prefix, text suffix, icon addons, actions, checkbox addons and all three sizes are shown.

  <input class="zak-input" id="locked" value="managed-by-policy" disabled/>
</div>

Usage

The focus ring lives on the group (:focus-within) so any segment receiving focus lights the field once.
For a purely decorative leading icon, .zak-input-wrap + .zak-icon is the lighter option.

One variant per card — the markup in each code tab is exactly what renders above it.

Field variants

Set the variant on the .zak-field wrapper — the textarea inherits the surface.

Sizes

<textarea class="zak-textarea" rows="3" placeholder="Medium"></textarea>
<textarea class="zak-textarea zak-textarea--lg" rows="3" placeholder="Large"></textarea>

Select

A native `<select>` — best mobile ergonomics, zero JS — styled with a custom chevron and generous end padding. It carries the same field surface as an input, so it composes inside `.zak-field` identically.

Determines the default review pool.

  <select class="zak-select" id="team">
    <option>Platform</option>
    <option>Design</option>
  </select>

</div>

  <option>Platform</option>
  <option>Design</option>
  <option>Data</option>
  <option>Infrastructure</option>
</select>

<!-- Small size -->
<select class="zak-select zak-input--sm" aria-label="Density">
  <option>Comfortable</option>
  <option>Compact</option>
</select>

<!-- Variants (on the wrapper or the control) -->
<select class="zak-select zak-select--filled" aria-label="Region">

</select>
<select class="zak-select zak-select--underline" aria-label="Theme">
  <option>Light</option>
</select>

<!-- Disabled -->
<select class="zak-select" disabled aria-label="Disabled">
  <option>Disabled</option>
</select>

Labelled field

Multi Select

Dropdown multi-select: a checkbox option list whose selections render as removable chips inside the field. Options and initial values come from JSON via `data-zak-source` and `data-zak-value` — no options are hard-coded in markup. Keyboard: focus the field and press Enter/Space to open, Escape to close.

Demo

Multi-value selection with removable tags.

<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-multiselect"
  data-zak-multiselect
  data-zak-source
  data-zak-value
  data-zak-placeholder="Select channels…"
></div>
<div class="zak-multiselect" data-zak-multiselect
     data-zak-source='[{"label":"Email","value":"email"},{"label":"Slack","value":"slack"},{"label":"PagerDuty","value":"pagerduty"}]'
     data-zak-value='["email","slack"]'
     data-zak-placeholder="Select channels…">
  <div class="zak-multiselect__field" role="combobox" aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">
    <span class="zak-multiselect__chips"></span>
    <span class="zak-multiselect__toggle" aria-hidden="true"><svg>…</svg></span>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-multiselect__panel" role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true" hidden></div>
</div>
The multiselect controller reads `data-zak-source`/`data-zak-value`, renders chips on load, builds the option panel on first open, and syncs selection on checkbox change or chip removal. Dispatches `zak:change` with the current value array.

Examples

One variant per card — the markup in each code tab is exactly what renders above it.

With a preselected count

Passing more values than fit shows an n selected summary via the placeholder slot.

<div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined" style="width:100%;max-width:24rem">
  <label class="zak-label">Team access</label>
  <div class="zak-multiselect" data-zak-multiselect
       data-zak-source='[{"label":"Engineering","value":"eng"},{"label":"Design","value":"design"},{"label":"Product","value":"product"},{"label":"Marketing","value":"marketing"}]'
       data-zak-value='["eng","design","product","marketing"]'>
    <div class="zak-multiselect__field" role="combobox" aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">
      <span class="zak-multiselect__chips"></span>
      <span class="zak-multiselect__count" aria-hidden="true"></span>
      <span class="zak-multiselect__toggle" aria-hidden="true"><svg class="zak-icon" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m6 9 6 6 6-6"/></svg></span>
    </div>
    <div class="zak-multiselect__panel" role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true" hidden></div>
  </div>
</div>

Small / large sizes

Combine with the shared field size modifiers for compact or prominent controls.

<div class="zak-stack zak-stack--md" style="width:100%;max-width:24rem">
  <div class="zak-multiselect" data-zak-multiselect
       data-zak-source='[{"label":"Sm","value":"sm"},{"label":"Option","value":"a"}]'
       data-zak-value='["sm"]'>
    <div class="zak-multiselect__field zak-input--sm" role="combobox" aria-haspopup="listbox" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0">
      <span class="zak-multiselect__chips"></span>

    </div>
    <div class="zak-multiselect__panel" role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true" hidden></div>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-multiselect" data-zak-multiselect
       data-zak-source='[{"label":"Lg","value":"lg"},{"label":"Option","value":"b"}]'
       data-zak-value='["lg"]'>

      <span class="zak-multiselect__chips"></span>

    </div>
    <div class="zak-multiselect__panel" role="listbox" aria-multiselectable="true" hidden></div>
  </div>

Checkbox

Custom-drawn checkbox with checked, indeterminate and disabled states. The control stays a real input for forms and assistive tech.

Demo

Checkbox with checked, indeterminate and disabled states.

<label class="zak-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked/>
  <span class="zak-check__label">
    Email me release notes
    <span class="zak-check__desc">Optional description</span>
  </span>
</label>

<script>
  // Partial selection (indeterminate)
  const box = document.getElementById('cb-ind');
  box.indeterminate = true;
</script>

<!-- Disabled -->
<label class="zak-check">
  <input type="checkbox" disabled checked/>
  <span class="zak-check__label">Managed by your organization</span>
</label>

Examples

One variant per card — the markup in each code tab is exactly what renders above it.

Label + description

The whole row is the click target; the description is secondary text under the label.

<label class="zak-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked/>
  <span class="zak-check__label">
    Email me release notes
    <span class="zak-check__desc">Sent to my verified address only</span>
  </span>
</label>

Indeterminate

The dash glyph is set through the JS property, never an attribute — bulk-selection header boxes need it.

<label class="zak-check">
  <input type="checkbox" id="selectAll"/>
  <span class="zak-check__label">Select all visible rows</span>
</label>

<script>
  // Partial selection is a property, not an attribute
  document.getElementById('selectAll').indeterminate = true;
</script>
const box = document.getElementById('selectAll');
box.indeterminate = true;   // dash glyph
box.indeterminate = false;  // back to checked / unchecked

Disabled

Locks the state, dims the row and leaves the tab order.

<label class="zak-check">
  <input type="checkbox" checked disabled/>
  <span class="zak-check__label">Two-factor auth</span>
</label>

Bare (table cells)

zak-check--bare drops the label text and tightens the box for grid and table selection columns.

<th class="zak-grid__check">
  <label class="zak-check zak-check--bare">
    <input type="checkbox" data-grid-check-all aria-label="Select all rows"/>
  </label>
</th>

  <span class="zak-file__icon">⬆</span>
  <span class="zak-file__title">Drop files here or <em>browse</em></span>
  <span class="zak-file__hint">PNG, JPG or PDF up to 10 MB each</span>
</label>

<!-- Single-file drop target (drop the multiple attribute) -->
<label class="zak-file" data-zak-dropzone>
  <input type="file" accept="image/*,.pdf"/>
  <span class="zak-file__title">Choose a file</span>
</label>

<!-- Completed file item -->
<div class="zak-file-list">
  <div class="zak-file-item">
    <span class="zak-file-item__meta">design-specs.pdf · 2.4 MB</span>
    <span class="zak-badge zak-badge--success"><span class="zak-badge__dot"></span>Complete</span>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--text zak-btn--icon zak-btn--sm" aria-label="Remove design-specs.pdf">✕</button>
  </div>

  <!-- Uploading file item with inline progress -->
  <div class="zak-file-item">
    <span class="zak-file-item__meta">screenshot.png · 840 KB</span>
    <span class="zak-progress zak-progress--sm"><span class="zak-progress__bar" style="--value:68%"></span></span>
  </div>
</div>
const zone = document.querySelector('[data-zak-dropzone]');
['dragenter', 'dragover'].forEach((type) =>
  zone.addEventListener(type, (event) => {
    event.preventDefault();
    zone.classList.add('is-dragover');
  })
);
zone.addEventListener('dragleave', () => zone.classList.remove('is-dragover'));
zone.addEventListener('drop', (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  zone.classList.remove('is-dragover');
  handleFiles(event.dataTransfer.files);
});

multiplebooleanfalseAllows selecting more than one file.
acceptstring—MIME filter, e.g. image/* or .pdf,.docx.
is-dragoverclass—Brand-tinted state applied during drag-over.

document.querySelectorAll('[data-zak-reveal]').forEach((button) => {
  button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    const input = button.parentElement.querySelector('input');
    const show = input.type === 'password';
    input.type = show ? 'text' : 'password';
    button.setAttribute('aria-label', show ? 'Hide password' : 'Show password');
  });
});

OTP Input

One-time passcode entry: six single-character boxes with auto-advance, single-press backspace clearing (Ctrl+A then Backspace clears the whole code) and paste support.

Demo

One-time passcode entry with auto-advance.

Code expires in 10 minutes. 
<!-- Inside a Form Field -->
<div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
  <label class="zak-label">One-time passcode</label>
  <div class="zak-otp" role="group" aria-label="One-time passcode">
    <input class="is-filled" inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" value="4" aria-label="Digit 1"/>
    <input inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" aria-label="Digit 2"/>
  </div>
  <span class="zak-hint">Code expires in 10 minutes.</span>
</div>

<!-- One box per digit; is-filled marks entered values -->
<div class="zak-otp" role="group" aria-label="One-time passcode">
  <input class="is-filled" inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" value="4" aria-label="Digit 1"/>
  <input class="is-filled" inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" value="8" aria-label="Digit 2"/>
  <input class="is-filled" inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" value="1" aria-label="Digit 3"/>
  <input inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" aria-label="Digit 4" autofocus/>
  <input inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" aria-label="Digit 5"/>
  <input inputmode="numeric" maxlength="1" aria-label="Digit 6"/>
</div>
const boxes = [...document.querySelectorAll('.zak-otp input')];
boxes.forEach((box, i) => {
  box.addEventListener('input', () => {
    box.classList.toggle('is-filled', box.value !== '');
    if (box.value && boxes[i + 1]) boxes[i + 1].focus();
  });
  box.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
    if (event.key === 'Backspace' && box.value) {
      event.preventDefault(); // one press erases the focused digit
      box.value = '';
      box.classList.remove('is-filled');
    } else if (event.key === 'Backspace' && !box.value && boxes[i - 1]) {
      event.preventDefault(); // empty box: clear and land on the previous digit
      boxes[i - 1].value = '';
      boxes[i - 1].classList.remove('is-filled');
      boxes[i - 1].focus();
    }
  });
  box.addEventListener('paste', (event) => {
    const digits = event.clipboardData.getData('text').replace(/\D/g, '');
    boxes.forEach((target, j) => {
      target.value = digits[j] ?? '';
      target.classList.toggle('is-filled', target.value !== '');
    });
    event.preventDefault();
  });
});

Tags Input

Free-form label entry: commit with Enter or comma, remove with Backspace or the chip close button, paste to import many at once.

Demo

Free-form label entry with chip management.

design-system enterprise a11y 
<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-tags"
  data-zak-tags
></div>
<!-- Committed chips plus a draft input -->
<div class="zak-tags" data-zak-tags>
  <span class="zak-tag">design-system <button class="zak-tag__x" aria-label="Remove design-system">✕</button></span>
  <span class="zak-tag">enterprise <button class="zak-tag__x" aria-label="Remove enterprise">✕</button></span>
  <span class="zak-tag">a11y <button class="zak-tag__x" aria-label="Remove a11y">✕</button></span>
  <input class="zak-tags__input" placeholder="Add label…" aria-label="Add label"/>
</div>
const root = document.querySelector('[data-zak-tags]');
const input = root.querySelector('.zak-tags__input');

function addTag(value) {
  const text = value.trim();
  if (!text) return;
  const chip = document.createElement('span');
  chip.className = 'zak-tag';
  chip.textContent = text + ' ';
  const remove = document.createElement('button');
  remove.className = 'zak-tag__x';
  remove.type = 'button';
  remove.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Remove ' + text);
  remove.textContent = '×';
  chip.append(remove);
  root.insertBefore(chip, input);
  input.value = '';
}

input.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key === 'Enter' || event.key === ',') { event.preventDefault(); addTag(input.value); }
  if (event.key === 'Backspace' && !input.value) root.querySelector('.zak-tag:last-of-type')?.remove();
});

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
data-zak-tagsattr—Marks the tags container for the behaviour module.
.zak-tags__inputelement—Entry point; flexes to fill remaining width.
Enter / ,interaction—Commits the current draft as a chip.
Backspaceinteraction—Removes the last chip when the draft is empty.

<div class="zak-box"
  data-zak-wizard
></div>
<!-- Wizard root: rail, one panel per step, shared actions. No init call needed -->
<div class="zak-box" data-zak-wizard>
  <!-- Step rail: is-done / is-active / upcoming, driven by the runtime -->
  <div class="zak-wizard__steps" role="list" aria-label="Checkout steps">
    <button class="zak-wizard__step is-active" type="button" role="listitem" data-zak-wizard-goto="0" aria-current="step">1 · Workspace</button>
    <button class="zak-wizard__step" type="button" role="listitem" data-zak-wizard-goto="1">2 · Billing</button>
    <button class="zak-wizard__step" type="button" role="listitem" data-zak-wizard-goto="2">3 · Review</button>
  </div>

  <!-- Panels: index matches the rail; every panel but the first starts hidden -->
  <div class="zak-wizard__panel" data-zak-wizard-panel="0">
    <div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
      <label class="zak-label" for="company">Company</label>
      <input class="zak-input" id="company" required/>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-wizard__panel" data-zak-wizard-panel="1" hidden>…</div>
  <div class="zak-wizard__panel" data-zak-wizard-panel="2" hidden>…</div>

  <!-- Actions: back is disabled on the first step, next validates then advances -->
  <div class="zak-wizard__actions">
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--text" type="button" data-zak-wizard-back disabled>Back</button>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled" type="button" data-zak-wizard-next>Continue</button>
  </div>
</div>
// The runtime fires one event per step change — use it to persist or gate
 document.querySelector('[data-zak-wizard]').addEventListener('zak:wizard', (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail.index, event.detail.action); // 0..n · 'next' | 'back' | 'goto' | 'complete'
});

Usage

The last step's Continue acts as Finish: it validates, marks every step done and emits action: "complete".

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
data-zak-wizardattr—Root that owns the rail, panels and actions.
data-zak-wizard-panel="i"attr—Step body; the runtime hides all but the active index.
data-zak-wizard-goto="i"attr—Rail button that jumps to a step (forward jumps validate first).
data-zak-wizard-nextattr—Advances after validating required fields in the leaving panel.
data-zak-wizard-backattr—Goes back one step; auto-disabled on the first panel.
is-done / is-activeclass—Step rail states, applied by the runtime; aria-current="step" tracks the active one.
zak:wizardevent—Fires with { index, total, action } on every change; action: "complete" on the final Continue.

Dynamic Field

Repeatable field groups: users add, remove and reorder rows. The runtime registers add, delete and HTML5 drag-reorder behaviour automatically — grab a row by its handle to move it.

Demo

Repeatable field groups users can add, remove and reorder.

  data-zak-repeater

<!-- Repeater root with a list and an add button -->
<div data-zak-repeater>
  <div class="zak-repeater" data-repeater-list>
    <div class="zak-repeater__row">
      <!-- Handle is the drag source: draggable="true" starts an HTML5 drag of the row -->
      <span class="zak-repeater__handle" draggable="true" aria-hidden="true">⠿</span>
      <input class="zak-input" value="admin@northwind.dev" aria-label="Email"/>
      <select class="zak-select" aria-label="Role">
        <option>Owner</option><option>Editor</option><option>Viewer</option>
      </select>
      <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--text zak-btn--icon" aria-label="Remove row" data-repeater-remove><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined zak-btn--sm" data-repeater-add><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Add member</button>
</div>
// No wiring needed — the delegated runtime handles add, remove and drag-reorder.
// Listen for the resulting order if you need to persist it:
const list = document.querySelector('[data-repeater-list]');
list.addEventListener('dragend', () => {
  console.log([...list.querySelectorAll('.zak-repeater__row input')].map((i) => i.value));
});

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
data-zak-repeaterattr—Root that groups the repeatable list.
data-repeater-addattr—Button that clones the last row (clears its inputs).
data-repeater-removeattr—Button that removes its row (minimum one kept).
.zak-repeater__handleelement—Set draggable="true" to drag-reorder the row via HTML5 DnD.
zak-repeater__row--draggingclass—Applied to the row in flight; styles the ghost target.

Validation

Validation states pair colour, an inline success/error icon inside the field, and a text message so meaning survives colorblindness. `aria-invalid` and live messages keep assistive tech informed. The icon treatment applies automatically to inputs, textareas, selects and password fields carrying `.is-valid`/`.is-invalid`.

Demo

Error, success and hint messaging patterns.

Enter a complete email address.
Available.
Region is required for compliance. 
<!-- Invalid field pairs colour with an icon + message -->
<div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
  <label class="zak-label" for="v-1">Work email</label>
  <input class="zak-input is-invalid" id="v-1" value="ada@northwind"
         aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="v-1-msg"/>
  <span class="zak-msg zak-msg--error" id="v-1-msg"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Enter a complete email address.</span>
</div>

<!-- Valid field -->
<div class="zak-field zak-field--outlined">
  <label class="zak-label" for="v-2">Workspace slug</label>
  <input class="zak-input is-valid" id="v-2" value="northwind-labs" aria-describedby="v-2-msg"/>
  <span class="zak-msg zak-msg--success" id="v-2-msg"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Available.</span>
</div>

<!-- Selects share the same states -->
<select class="zak-select is-invalid" aria-invalid="true">…</select>
input.addEventListener('blur', () => {
  const valid = input.checkValidity();
  input.classList.toggle('is-invalid', !valid);
  input.setAttribute('aria-invalid', String(!valid));
});

Links to the message (aria-describedby)

Every state is announced, not just coloured — the control references its message id so screen readers read it after the field name.

Region is required for compliance. 
<select class="zak-select is-invalid" aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="region-msg">…</select>
<span class="zak-msg zak-msg--error" id="region-msg">Region is required for compliance.</span>

Live message (role="alert")

When an error appears after a blur or submit, promote the message with role="alert" so it is announced immediately.

<span class="zak-msg zak-msg--error" id="coupon-msg" role="alert">This code has expired.</span>

Calendar

A generated calendar surface in one container. Declaring `data-zak-calendar` is the only markup — the runtime builds the month grid, weekday row and day cells; the surrounding field and floating panel are the standard picker chrome. Choosing a day writes the formatted value back and closes the panel.

Month grid with single-date selection.

Focus or click the field to open the calendar.

      <div data-zak-calendar="2026-06-18" data-zak-cal-today="2026-06-17"></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

One variant per card — the markup in each code tab is exactly what renders above it.

Single month grid

One attribute generates the header, weekday row and 42 day cells.

<div data-zak-calendar="2026-06-18" data-zak-cal-today="2026-06-17"></div>

Range selection

data-zak-cal-select="range" turns the grid into a two-endpoint picker; --months="2" shows a span side by side.

<div data-zak-calendar="2026-06-09..2026-06-24"
     data-zak-cal-select="range"
     data-zak-cal-months="2"
     data-zak-cal-today="2026-06-17"></div>

Weeks view

data-zak-cal-view="weeks" lists ISO week rows instead of a day grid.

<div data-zak-calendar="2026-06-15"
     data-zak-cal-view="weeks"
     data-zak-cal-weeks="6"
     data-zak-cal-today="2026-06-17"></div>

Min / max bounds

Days outside the bounds render disabled and stay out of the tab order.

<div data-zak-calendar="2026-06-18"
     data-zak-cal-min="2026-06-01"
     data-zak-cal-max="2026-06-30"
     data-zak-cal-today="2026-06-17"></div>

Usage

Prefer the one-line field form: <input class="zak-input" data-zak-datepicker> generates all of this at runtime.
Day cells keep tabindex="-1" — the grid implements a single roving tab stop; arrows move focus.
Weekday headers are aria-hidden; each day cell carries its full date as the accessible name.

Chip

Compact tokens for filters, tags and selections. Chips come in static, interactive (selectable) and removable flavors — removal is delegated so the chip itself stays a simple token.

Demo

Removable or selectable compact tokens.

Production eu-central-1 v2.4.1
Brand Success Warning Danger Info Neutral
Brand Success Warning Danger Info
design-system a11y release-2.4 
<!-- Tones: one modifier per semantic colour, theme-aware through the tokens -->
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--primary">Brand</span>
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--success">Success</span>
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--warning">Warning</span>
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--danger">Danger</span>
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--info">Info</span>
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--neutral">Neutral</span>

<!-- Outline shape: transparent surface, tone kept in text and border -->
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--danger zak-chip--outline">Danger</span>

<!-- Interactive chip: .zak-chip--interactive -->
<button class="zak-chip zak-chip--interactive" type="button" aria-pressed="false">Warnings</button>

<!-- Selected: is-active -->
<button class="zak-chip zak-chip--interactive is-active" type="button" aria-pressed="true">Errors</button>

<!-- Removable: .zak-chip__x must name its chip -->
<span class="zak-chip zak-chip--info">design-system
  <button class="zak-chip__x" type="button" aria-label="Remove design-system">✕</button>
</span>
// Removal is delegated from the list container
list.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const x = event.target.closest('.zak-chip__x');
  if (!x) return;
  const chip = x.closest('[data-zak-chip]');
  chip.remove();
  announce(`Removed ${chip.textContent.trim()}`);
});

Rating

Star rating for input and read-only display in three sizes. Interactive instances toggle `is-on` per star; the numeric value stays in sync via `aria-label`.

Demo

Star rating input and read-only display.

3.0
4.0
4.5 · 128 reviews
<!-- Sizes: --sm / --lg (md is the default) -->
<div class="zak-rating zak-rating--sm" role="img" aria-label="Rated 3 out of 5">
  <!-- Awarded star: .zak-rating__star.is-on -->
  <span class="zak-rating__star is-on">★</span>
  <span class="zak-rating__star is-on">★</span>
  <span class="zak-rating__star is-on">★</span>
  <span class="zak-rating__star">★</span>
</div>

<!-- Numeric companion: .zak-rating__value -->
<span class="zak-rating__value">4.0</span>
rating.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const star = event.target.closest('.zak-rating__star');
  if (!star) return;
  const index = [...rating.children].indexOf(star);
  [...rating.querySelectorAll('.zak-rating__star')].forEach((s, i) =>
    s.classList.toggle('is-on', i <= index)
  );
  rating.setAttribute('aria-label', `Rated ${index + 1} out of 5`);
});

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
.zak-rating__star.is-onclass—Amber 500 fill for awarded stars.
--sm / --lgmodifiermdIcon sizes 0.95rem / 1.15rem / 1.7rem.
.zak-rating__valueelement—Numeric companion — never rely on stars alone.

header.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const next = header.dataset.dir === 'asc' ? 'desc' : 'asc';
  header.dataset.dir = next;
  th.setAttribute('aria-sort', next === 'asc' ? 'ascending' : 'descending');
  sortRows(column, next);
});

button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const open = button.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  button.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!open));
  button.classList.toggle('is-open', !open);
  button.closest('tr').nextElementSibling.hidden = open;
});

<!-- Parent row: --depth sets the indent, data-level drives collapse math -->
<tr data-level="0" aria-expanded="true">
  <td class="zak-table__indent" style="--depth:0">
    <!-- .zak-table__tree keeps toggle, label and badge on one baseline -->
    <span class="zak-table__tree">
      <button class="zak-table__toggle" type="button" aria-label="Collapse platform"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>

  <td class="zak-table__num">48%</td>

<!-- Child row: one level deeper -->

<!-- Grandchild row -->

<!-- Collapsed children simply carry hidden; the caret rotation is pure CSS -->
<tr data-level="1" hidden><td class="zak-table__indent" style="--depth:1">postgres-cluster</td></tr>

Collapsed branch

Children of a closed branch just carry hidden; the caret rotation and the aria-label swap come from aria-expanded alone.

<!-- Closed parent: aria-expanded="false", every deeper row hidden -->
<tr data-level="0" aria-expanded="false">
  <td class="zak-table__indent" style="--depth:0">
    <span class="zak-table__tree">
      <button class="zak-table__toggle" type="button" aria-label="Expand infra"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>

// The runtime hides exactly one descendant block: everything deeper than
// the toggled row, up to the next row at the same or a shallower level.
toggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const row = toggle.closest('tr');
  const open = row.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  row.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!open));
  const level = Number(row.dataset.level);

  for (let n = row.nextElementSibling; n; n = n.nextElementSibling) {
    if (Number(n.dataset.level) <= level) break;
    n.hidden = open;
  }
});

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
--depthcustom property0Indent level in rem multiples of 1.25; one per hierarchy step.
data-levelattr—Numeric depth; the runtime hides rows deeper than the toggled row.
aria-expandedattr—Parent state; drives the caret rotation and the aria-label swap.
.zak-table__indentclass—Cell that receives the depth-driven start padding.
.zak-table__treeclass—Inline-flex row: toggle, label and badge share one baseline.
.zak-table__toggleclass—Caret button; the row remains the click target.
[data-zak-table-tree]attr—Marks the wrapper whose rows are collapse-enabled.
.zak-table__numclass—Right-aligned numerics stay aligned across levels.

pagination.addEventListener('click', (event) => {
  const btn = event.target.closest('.zak-page-btn');
  if (!btn || btn.disabled) return;
  pagination.querySelectorAll('.zak-page-btn').forEach((b) => {
    b.classList.toggle('is-active', b === btn);
    b.toggleAttribute('aria-current', b === btn);
  });
  loadPage(Number(btn.textContent));
});

// indeterminate is a property, never an attribute — set it after each toggle
const boxes = [...table.querySelectorAll('tbody input[type="checkbox"]')];
const checked = boxes.filter((box) => box.checked);

checkAll.checked = checked.length === boxes.length;
checkAll.indeterminate = checked.length > 0 && checked.length < boxes.length;

// Keep the row fill in sync with its checkbox
boxes.forEach((box) =>
  box.addEventListener('change', () => box.closest('tr').classList.toggle('is-selected', box.checked)),
);

  <span class="zak-spinner zak-spinner--sm"></span> Fetching rows…

<!-- zak:gridrequest — one integration point for every state change -->
grid.addEventListener('zak:gridrequest', async () => {
  const res = await fetch('/api/members');
  renderRows(await res.json());
  updateRangeLabel(result.from, result.to, result.total);
});

<!-- range label — always echo the server's totals -->
<span class="zak-grid__count" data-grid-count>1–5 of 24</span>
grid.addEventListener('zak:gridrequest', async () => {
  grid.classList.add('is-loading');           // overlay via [data-grid-loading]
  const res = await fetch(`/api/members?${params}`);
  renderRows(await res.json());               // swap tbody
  updateRangeLabel(result.from, result.to, result.total);
  grid.classList.remove('is-loading');
});

Editable Data Grid

In-cell editing: click a cell, type, press Tab or click away to commit. Invalid values flash the danger ring and keep focus for correction.

Demo

In-cell editing with validation affordances.

TeamRoleLocationBalance
Fetching rows…
<!-- contenteditable="true" — editable cells; Tab moves to the next cell -->
<td class="zak-grid__cell-edit" contenteditable="true" data-value="Editor">Editor</td>

<!-- .zak-grid__cell-edit — hover surface + focus ring for the cell value -->
<td class="zak-grid__cell-edit" contenteditable="true">Editor</td>

<!-- is-invalid — danger focus ring keeps focus until the value parses -->
<td class="zak-grid__cell-edit is-invalid" contenteditable="true">300%</td>
cell.addEventListener('blur', () => {
  if (cell.textContent.trim() === cell.dataset.value) return;
  if (!validate(cell.textContent)) {
    cell.classList.add('is-invalid');   // brand → danger focus ring
    cell.focus();
    return;
  }
  commit(cell.dataset.row, cell.dataset.col, cell.textContent);
});

handle.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => {
  handle.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId);
  handle.classList.add('is-active');
  const startX = e.clientX;
  const startW = th.offsetWidth;
  handle.addEventListener('pointermove', (ev) => {
    th.style.width = `${Math.max(80, startW + ev.clientX - startX)}px`;
  }, { once: false });
});

<!-- data-grid-filter — named like its column key; empty value means no constraint -->
<select class="zak-select" data-grid-filter="team" aria-label="Filter by team">
  <option value="">All teams</option>
  <option selected>Platform</option>

filters.forEach((select) => {
  select.addEventListener('change', () => {
    state.filters[select.dataset.gridFilter] = select.value;
    state.page = 1;                     // always reset to page one
    applyFilters();                     // recompute state.filtered
    render();                           // rows + count + pager
  });
});

Dropdown

The trigger-anchored panel. Hosts either a `role="menu"` list of items with shortcuts, or a richer content surface (form fields, links, one primary action). Panels align to either edge with `--end` and light-dismiss on outside click or Escape.

Demo

Trigger-anchored panel — menu items with shortcuts, or rich content.

Share document
<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-dropdown"
  data-zak-dropdown
></div>
<!-- Wrapper + trigger + panel: the runtime contract in overlays.ts -->
<div class="zak-dropdown" data-zak-dropdown>
  <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled" type="button" data-zak-toggle="dropdown"
          aria-expanded="false" aria-haspopup="dialog">Share ▾</button>

  <!-- aria-haspopup="dialog" — a rich panel is a dialog, not a menu -->
  <div class="zak-dropdown__panel" hidden style="width:21rem">
    <div class="zak-stack zak-stack--md">
      <input class="zak-input" value="zakui.dev/d/4f31c" readonly aria-label="Share link"/>
      <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled" type="button" style="width:100%">Copy link</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- .zak-dropdown__panel--end — right-aligns the panel for edge triggers -->
<div class="zak-dropdown">
  <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined" type="button" data-zak-toggle="dropdown" aria-expanded="false">Options</button>
  <div class="zak-dropdown__panel zak-dropdown__panel--end" hidden>…</div>
</div>

<!-- light dismiss: outside click and Esc close; focus returns to the trigger -->
// data-zak-toggle="dropdown" flips the sibling panel and the wrapper state
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const open = button.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
  button.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!open));
  panel.hidden = open;
  wrapper.classList.toggle('is-open', !open);
});

// Light dismiss: click outside, or Escape (focus returns to the trigger)
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  if (!wrapper.contains(e.target)) close();
});
document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key === 'Escape') close();
});

tablist.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  const i = tabs.indexOf(document.activeElement);
  if (event.key === 'ArrowRight') tabs[(i + 1) % tabs.length].focus();
  if (event.key === 'ArrowLeft') tabs[(i - 1 + tabs.length) % tabs.length].focus();
  if (event.key === 'Home') tabs[0].focus();
  if (event.key === 'End') tabs[tabs.length - 1].focus();
});

<!-- Scroll-spy: IntersectionObserver with a reading band (see JS) -->
<!-- Smooth scrolling: html { scroll-behavior: smooth } -->
// Scroll-spy: highlight the section owning the viewport band
const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
  entries.forEach((entry) => {
    if (!entry.isIntersecting) return;
    links.forEach((link) => {
      const active = link.hash === '#' + entry.target.id;
      link.classList.toggle('is-active', active);
      link.toggleAttribute('aria-current', active);
    });
  });
}, { rootMargin: '-20% 0px -70% 0px' });

sections.forEach((section) => observer.observe(section));

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
.zak-anchor-nav__link.is-activeclass—Brand text + 2px leading border.
IntersectionObserverapi—rootMargin shapes a reading band, not raw visibility.
scroll-behavior: smoothcss—Respect prefers-reduced-motion before enabling.

Toast

Transient notifications stacked in the bottom-right region: 5s autohide that pauses while the pointer or focus rests on the toast, a spring entry and a close affordance — Bootstrap-style behaviour on native APIs.

Demo

Transient notifications with auto-dismiss.

Changes saved
Deployment config updated 2s ago.
<!-- The fixed stack lives in a persistent region -->
<div class="zak-toast-region zak-toast-region--bottom-end">
  <div class="zak-toast zak-toast--success" role="status">
    <span class="zak-toast__icon"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></span>
    <div class="zak-toast__body">
      <div class="zak-toast__title">Changes saved</div>
      <div class="zak-toast__desc">Deployment config updated 2s ago.</div>
    </div>
    <button class="zak-toast__close" type="button" aria-label="Dismiss" data-zak-dismiss><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- .zak-toast-region: fixed stack — --top-end / --bottom-start reposition it -->
<!-- Fire from script — tone info · success · warning · danger; opts { duration, desc } -->
<script>
  window.ZakUI.toast('Deployment started', 'success');
  // duration:0 pins the toast until it is dismissed; autohide pauses on hover / focus
  window.ZakUI.toast('API token expires in 3 days', 'warning', {
    duration: 0,
    desc: 'Rotate it to keep CI pipelines green.',
  });
</script>

<!-- .is-leaving plays the slide-out; remove after animationend -->

<!-- Or fire from markup with no JavaScript at all: the runtime reads the
     attributes off any element you click -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined zak-btn--sm" type="button"
        data-zak-toast="Deployment started" data-zak-toast-tone="success">Fire a live toast</button>

<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--text zak-btn--sm" type="button"
        data-zak-toast="API token expires in 3 days" data-zak-toast-tone="warning"
        data-zak-toast-desc="Rotate it to keep CI pipelines green."
        data-zak-toast-duration="0">Pinned with description</button>
// One shared region, appended lazily — bottom-right by default
const region = document.querySelector('.zak-toast-region') ?? createRegion();

export function toast(title, tone = 'default', { duration = 5000, desc } = {}) {
  const el = buildToast(title, tone, desc);          // .zak-toast markup
  region.append(el);
  if (duration > 0) scheduleAutohide(el, duration);  // pauses on hover/focus
  el.querySelector('[aria-label="Dismiss"]').onclick = () => dismiss(el);
}

function dismiss(el) {
  el.classList.add('is-leaving');                    // 220ms exit animation
  el.addEventListener('animationend', () => el.remove(), { once: true });
}

Scripted toast

ZakUI.toast() builds and queues the same markup — useful from a fetch handler or an event listener.

Build failed
Step “test:unit” exited with code 1.
<!-- The region is created on first call — bottom-end by default -->
<script>
  ZakUI.toast('Build failed', 'danger', {
    desc: 'Step “test:unit” exited with code 1.',
    duration: 0,               // 0 pins it until dismissed
  });
</script>
// Same call through the controller class — tone is positional
ZakToast.show('Build failed', 'danger', {
  desc: 'Step “test:unit” exited with code 1.',
  duration: 8000,
});

// The autohide countdown pauses on hover and focus, then resumes

// Reposition the stack before the first toast appears — the runtime reuses it
document.body.insertAdjacentHTML(
  'beforeend',
  '<div class="zak-toast-region zak-toast-region--top-start" aria-live="polite"></div>',
);

Usage

The autohide countdown pauses the moment the user hovers or focuses a toast — reading time never races the timer.

  duration: 4000,                 // 0 pins it; hover/focus pauses the countdown

});

  <span class="zak-snackbar__msg">Draft deleted</span>
  <!-- The action inherits the secondary-300 link tone from .zak-snackbar -->
  <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--link zak-btn--sm" type="button">Undo</button>
</div>

Message only

When nothing can be undone, the message stands alone — the region still announces it politely.

Message moved to Trash 
<div class="zak-snackbar" role="status">
  <span class="zak-snackbar__msg">Message moved to Trash</span>
</div>

Fired from attributes

Zero inline JavaScript: data-zak-snackbar carries the message, the companion attributes carry the action label and the lifetime.

<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined zak-btn--sm" type="button"
        data-zak-snackbar="Draft deleted" data-zak-snackbar-action="Undo">With Undo</button>

<!-- data-zak-snackbar-duration="0" — stays until the action is used -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--text zak-btn--sm" type="button"
        data-zak-snackbar="Sync paused" data-zak-snackbar-duration="0">Pinned</button>

Action callback

onAction runs before the snackbar leaves; without it the click emits zak:snackbar-action so any listener can react.

Invite revoked for samuel@zakui.dev 
<script>
  ZakUI.snackbar('Invite revoked', {
    actionLabel: 'Undo',
    onAction: () => restoreInvite(),   // runs, then the snackbar leaves
    duration: 0,                       // wait for the user instead of a timer
  });
</script>
// Controller-class entry point over the same runtime
ZakSnackbar.show('Draft deleted', { actionLabel: 'Undo' });

// Clicking an action with no callback bound emits the event instead
document.addEventListener('zak:snackbar-action', (event) => {
  console.log(event.detail.action, '→', event.detail.message);
});

Usage

Snackbars carry exactly one action; if the operation needs more, promote it to a toast with actions.

<!-- Size modifiers: .zak-modal--sm (24rem) · .zak-modal--lg (46rem) · .zak-modal--xl (64rem) -->
<dialog class="zak-modal zak-modal--lg" id="changelog" aria-labelledby="changelog-title">
  <div class="zak-modal__header">
    <div class="zak-modal__title" id="changelog-title">What’s new in 2.4</div>
    <button class="zak-modal__close" type="button" aria-label="Close" data-zak-close>✕</button>

// Trigger contract — works for any dialog-based overlay
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const trigger = e.target.closest('[data-zak-toggle][data-zak-target]');
  if (trigger) {
    document.querySelector(trigger.dataset.zakTarget)?.showModal();
  }
  const closer = e.target.closest('[data-zak-close]');
  if (closer) closer.closest('dialog')?.close();
});

// Click on ::backdrop targets the <dialog> itself
dialog.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  if (e.target === dialog) dialog.close();
});

Full-height slide-over for editing without leaving context — the list stays visible behind. Header, scrollable body and pinned footer form the three-row shell.

Side sheet for forms and details.

<div class="zak-flex" style="justify-content:center">
  <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--filled" type="button" data-zak-toggle="drawer" data-zak-target="#profile">Edit profile</button>
</div>

<dialog class="zak-drawer" id="profile" aria-labelledby="profile-title">
  <div class="zak-drawer__header">
    <span class="zak-drawer__title" id="profile-title">Edit profile</span>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--ghost zak-btn--icon zak-btn--sm" type="button" aria-label="Close" style="margin-inline-start:auto" data-zak-close>✕</button>
  </div>

  <!-- .zak-drawer__body — the only scrolling region; header and footer stay pinned -->
  <div class="zak-drawer__body">
    <div class="zak-field">
      <label class="zak-label" for="profile-name">Full name</label>
      <input class="zak-input" id="profile-name" value="Abdul Shaikh"/>
    </div>
  </div>

  <!-- margin-inline-end:auto pushes a leading action away from the save cluster -->
  <div class="zak-drawer__footer">
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--ghost" type="button" style="color:var(--zak-danger-text);margin-inline-end:auto">Delete account</button>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--ghost" type="button" data-zak-close>Cancel</button>
    <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--primary" type="button" data-zak-close>Save changes</button>
  </div>
</dialog>

<!-- [open] animation: 40px slide-in on the slow duration token, ease-out -->
<!-- Edge: .zak-drawer--right (default) or .zak-drawer--left — mirrors the border -->
// Same trigger contract — the drawer is a <dialog> with slide-in CSS
document.querySelector('[data-zak-toggle="drawer"]')
  .addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    document.querySelector(e.currentTarget.dataset.zakTarget).showModal();
  });

// Unsaved-changes guard before closing
dialog.addEventListener('cancel', (e) => {
  if (formDirty && !confirm('Discard unsaved changes?')) e.preventDefault();
});

Popover

Light-dismiss popups built on the Popover API: Escape, click-outside and top-layer stacking come native. The runtime anchors the panel to its trigger — below-start by default, flipping to the side with room — so it never detaches from the control that opened it.

Demo

Anchored rich content using the native popover API.

Notify me about
Requested placement is the inline end; the runtime keeps it there only while it fits.
<!-- popovertarget wires the trigger to the panel by id -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined" type="button" popovertarget="notify">Notification settings</button>

<!-- popover="auto" — light dismiss: Esc, outside click and top-layer stacking -->
<div class="zak-popover" popover id="notify" aria-labelledby="notify-title">
  <div id="notify-title" style="font-weight:var(--zak-weight-semibold);font-size:var(--zak-text-sm);margin-block-end:var(--zak-space-3)">Notify me about</div>
  <div class="zak-stack zak-stack--sm">
    <label class="zak-switch zak-switch--sm"><input type="checkbox" checked role="switch"/> Deployments</label>
    <label class="zak-switch zak-switch--sm"><input type="checkbox" role="switch"/> Incident alerts</label>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- .zak-popover — elevated surface the runtime anchors to its trigger -->
<!-- data-zak-placement="side[-align]" — side: top|bottom|left|right · align: start|center|end (default bottom) -->
<div class="zak-popover" popover id="notes" data-zak-placement="end" aria-label="Cell notes">…</div>

<!-- ::backdrop: none — popovers never dim the page; that is modal-dialog only -->
<!-- toggle event fires with newState on open/close — position the panel on open -->
// Native toggling — no JS needed for open/close at all
// <button popovertarget="panel-id"> + <div popover id="panel-id">

// Popovers never get a ::backdrop — that treatment is modal-dialog only.
// Placement is anchored to the trigger, then clamped into the viewport:
// measure the panel after the open styles apply (rAF), flip when clipped.
document.addEventListener('toggle', (event) => {
  const popover = event.target;
  if (popover.newState !== 'open') return;

  const trigger = popover.invoker ?? document.querySelector('[popovertarget="' + popover.id + '"]');
  const rect = trigger.getBoundingClientRect();
  const gap = 8, edge = 12;
  let placement = popover.dataset.zakPlacement ?? 'bottom';

  // Flip to the opposite side when the preferred one is clipped by the viewport
  const below = rect.bottom + gap + popover.offsetHeight <= innerHeight - edge;
  if (placement === 'bottom' && !below) placement = 'top';

  const top = placement === 'bottom' ? rect.bottom + gap : rect.top - gap - popover.offsetHeight;
  popover.style.left = Math.min(Math.max(edge, rect.left), innerWidth - popover.offsetWidth - edge) + 'px';
  popover.style.top = Math.max(edge, top) + 'px';
});

Placement

data-zak-placement takes a side with an optional alignment — top, bottom, left, right plus -start / -center / -end. The runtime keeps the request only while it fits, then flips to the first side with room.

Anchored above, left-aligned to the trigger.
Anchored above, right-aligned to the trigger.
Anchored below, left-aligned — the default.
Anchored below, right-aligned to the trigger.
Anchored to the inline-start edge.
Anchored to the inline-end edge.

<span class="zak-tooltip zak-tooltip--bottom">
  <button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined zak-btn--icon" type="button" aria-label="Information"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
  <span class="zak-tooltip__bubble" role="tooltip">Below the trigger</span>
</span>
.zak-tooltip { position: relative; display: inline-flex; }

.zak-tooltip__bubble {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: calc(100% + 0.45rem);
  left: 50%;
  transform: translateX(-50%) translateY(2px) scale(0.97);
  opacity: 0;
  pointer-events: none;
  transition: opacity var(--zak-duration-fast),
    transform var(--zak-duration-fast) var(--zak-ease-out);
}

.zak-tooltip:hover .zak-tooltip__bubble,
.zak-tooltip:focus-within .zak-tooltip__bubble {
  opacity: 1;
  transform: translateX(-50%) translateY(0) scale(1);
}

/* .zak-tooltip--bottom drops the bubble below and flips the arrow */
.zak-tooltip--bottom .zak-tooltip__bubble { bottom: auto; top: calc(100% + 0.45rem); }

  <button class="zak-context-menu__item" type="button" role="menuitem"><svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg> Open <kbd class="zak-kbd">↵</kbd></button>

</div>
zone.addEventListener('contextmenu', (e) => {
  e.preventDefault();
  openMenu(e.clientX, e.clientY);
});

function openMenu(x, y) {
  menu.hidden = false;
  const r = menu.getBoundingClientRect();
  menu.style.left = Math.min(x, innerWidth - r.width - 8) + 'px';
  menu.style.top = Math.min(y, innerHeight - r.height - 8) + 'px';
  menu.querySelector('[role="menuitem"]').focus();
}

document.addEventListener('pointerdown', (e) => {
  if (!menu.contains(e.target)) menu.hidden = true;
});

Accordion

Stacked FAQ / settings sections where one answer stays open at a time. The trigger owns aria-expanded, the panel owns hidden — and the chevron rotates off the aria state alone.

Demo

Stacked expand/collapse panels.

You are billed for members who signed in during the last 30 days. Invited members start counting on their first login — no charge for scoped guests.
Yes — the entire component layer is dependency-free ES modules. Ship the CSS tokens and the behaviour scripts from your own origin; nothing calls home.

<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-accordion"
  data-zak-accordion="single"
></div>
<!-- data-zak-accordion — behaviour root; "single" keeps one item open -->
<div class="zak-accordion" data-zak-accordion="single">
  <div class="zak-accordion__item">
    <!-- aria-expanded + hidden: state lives in ARIA, CSS reads it — no class juggling -->
    <button class="zak-accordion__trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="true" aria-controls="a1">How does seat-based billing work? <svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
    <div class="zak-accordion__panel" id="a1">You are billed for members who signed in during the last 30 days.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="zak-accordion__item">
    <button class="zak-accordion__trigger" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="a2">Can I self-host the grid runtime? <svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>
    <div class="zak-accordion__panel" id="a2" hidden>Yes — the component layer is dependency-free ES modules.</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- .zak-accordion__panel — indented body copy; display:none when hidden -->
<!-- chevron transform: rotates 180deg from aria-expanded="true", no JS class toggling -->
<!-- data-zak-accordion="multi" allows several panels open at once -->
wrapper.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const trigger = e.target.closest('.zak-accordion__trigger');
  if (!trigger) return;
  const panel = document.getElementById(trigger.getAttribute('aria-controls'));
  const open = trigger.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';

  // data-zak-accordion="single" — close whatever was open before
  if (wrapper.dataset.zakAccordion === 'single' && !open) {
    wrapper.querySelectorAll('.zak-accordion__trigger[aria-expanded="true"]')
      .forEach((other) => {
        other.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        document.getElementById(other.getAttribute('aria-controls')).hidden = true;
      });
  }

  trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(!open));
  panel.hidden = open;
});

Collapse

One animated region for everything else. The modern grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr technique animates to auto height without measuring, and it stays interruptible mid-flight.

Demo

Animated show/hide region.

Traffic fails over automatically when p95 breaches 800 ms.
<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined"
  data-zak-toggle="collapse"
  data-zak-target="#advanced"
></button>
<!-- data-zak-toggle="collapse" — trigger contract; pair with data-zak-target="#advanced" -->
<button class="zak-btn zak-btn--outlined" type="button" aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="advanced" data-zak-toggle="collapse" data-zak-target="#advanced">Advanced options <svg class="zak-icon" aria-hidden="true">…</svg></button>

<!-- .zak-collapse.is-open flips grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr — height-agnostic.
     The direct child is the clip layer (padding-free); [hidden] is applied by the
     runtime when the closing transition ends, so no margin or border lingers. -->
<div class="zak-collapse" id="advanced" hidden>
  <div>
    <label class="zak-switch"><input type="checkbox" role="switch"/> Zero-downtime deploys</label>
    <label class="zak-switch"><input type="checkbox" role="switch"/> Canary traffic</label>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- interruption-safe: the grid-row animation re-targets smoothly mid-transition -->
<!-- inner padding rule: padding lives on the child, never the grid container -->
.zak-collapse {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-rows: 0fr;
  transition: grid-template-rows var(--zak-duration-base) var(--zak-ease-standard);
}

/* Clip layer — must stay padding-free or the closed state leaves a sliver */
.zak-collapse > * { overflow: hidden; min-height: 0; }

.zak-collapse.is-open { grid-template-rows: 1fr; }

/* Fully closed: applied by the runtime when the closing transition ends */
.zak-collapse[hidden] { display: none; }
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const trigger = e.target.closest('[data-zak-toggle="collapse"]');
  if (!trigger) return;
  const region = document.querySelector(trigger.dataset.zakTarget);
  const open = !region.classList.contains('is-open');
  trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(open));

  if (open) {
    region.hidden = false;
    // one unstyled frame so the transition has a 0fr starting box
    requestAnimationFrame(() => region.classList.add('is-open'));
    return;
  }

  region.classList.remove('is-open');
  // take it out of the layout only once the row has finished collapsing
  region.addEventListener('transitionend', (ev) => {
    if (ev.target === region && ev.propertyName === 'grid-template-rows' && !open) region.hidden = true;
  });
});

Details

The native <details> element — zero JavaScript, browser-managed state, and content that plays nicely with in-page find. The chevron rotates 90° off the [open] attribute.

Demo

Native details/summary disclosure.

What counts as an active seat?
A seat is active when a member signs in at least once every 30 days. Guest collaborators with scoped link access never consume a seat.
Can I change plans mid-cycle?
Yes. Upgrades apply instantly and are prorated to the day; downgrades take effect at the next renewal. Usage beyond the new limit is never billed retroactively.
Where is my data stored?
Primary storage is eu-west-1 with hot standby in eu-central-1. US workspaces pin to us-east-1. Region is fixed at workspace creation.

<details class="zak-details" open>
  <summary>▸ What counts as an active seat?</summary>
  <div class="zak-details__body">A seat is active when a member signs in at least once every 30 days.</div>
</details>

<!-- [open] — the attribute drives the chevron rotation via CSS only -->
<details class="zak-details">
  <summary>▸ Can I change plans mid-cycle?</summary>
  <div class="zak-details__body">Upgrades apply instantly and are prorated to the day.</div>
</details>

<!-- name="group" — group details elements for exclusive accordion behaviour -->
<details class="zak-details" name="faq">
  <summary>▸ Where is my data stored?</summary>
  <div class="zak-details__body">Primary storage is eu-west-1 with hot standby in eu-central-1.</div>
</details>

<!-- list-style: none hides the default triangle; a chevron icon is shipped instead -->
.zak-details > summary { list-style: none; cursor: pointer; }

.zak-details > summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }

.zak-details > summary .zak-icon {
  transition: transform var(--zak-duration-fast);
}

.zak-details[open] > summary .zak-icon { transform: rotate(90deg); }

Usage

Content inside details is indexable by browsers and assistive tech even when collapsed — ideal for FAQ blocks and changelog entries.

Show More / Show Less

Line-clamped copy with a soft fade and a single toggle. Cards stay scannable; long prose expands in place without navigating away.

Demo

Clamped text with expand control.

ZAKUIKit 2.4 focuses on the Data Grid and AI surfaces. Virtual scroll now renders 100k rows with a stable scroll position, the streaming response primitive graduated from beta, and popovers gained native light-dismiss handling. The token layer adds density modes at the app root, container-query toolbars collapse gracefully below 34rem, and every overlay moved onto the native dialog element — cutting the behaviour bundle by a third while improving focus management.

<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-showmore"
  data-zak-showmore
></div>
<!-- data-zak-showmore — root hook; .is-open releases the line clamp -->
<div class="zak-showmore" data-zak-showmore style="width:100%;max-width:36rem">

  <!-- --lines custom prop: -webkit-line-clamp: var(--lines, 3) -->
  <p class="zak-showmore__text" style="--lines:3;margin:0">ZAKUIKit 2.4 focuses on the Data Grid and AI surfaces. Virtual scroll now renders 100k rows with a stable scroll position, the streaming response primitive graduated from beta, and popovers gained native light-dismiss handling.</p>

  <!-- .zak-showmore__fade — gradient veil above the toggle; hidden once open -->
  <span class="zak-showmore__fade" aria-hidden="true"></span>

  <!-- aria-expanded on the toggle announces state; the label swaps to “Show less” -->
  <button class="zak-showmore__toggle zak-btn zak-btn--link zak-btn--sm" type="button" aria-expanded="false" data-zak-showmore-toggle>Show more</button>
</div>
const wrapper = document.querySelector('[data-zak-showmore]');
const toggle = wrapper.querySelector('[data-zak-showmore-toggle]');

toggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const open = wrapper.classList.toggle('is-open');
  toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', String(open));
  toggle.textContent = open ? 'Show less' : 'Show more';
});

    <!-- prev/next cycle the set; arrows sit on the image edges, vertically centred -->

    <button class="zak-lightbox__btn zak-lightbox__btn--next" type="button" aria-label="Next image" data-lightbox-next>›</button>

// One dialog serves the whole grid — no per-image overlays
grid.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const item = e.target.closest('[data-gallery-item]');
  if (!item) return;

  // Snapshot the whole set so prev/next can cycle it
  const items = [...scope.querySelectorAll('[data-gallery-item]')];
  state = { items, index: items.indexOf(item) };

  // Safe DOM swap — clone the artwork, no HTML parsing
  stage.replaceChildren(items[state.index].querySelector('.zak-img-ph').cloneNode(true));
  lightbox.showModal();
});

// Arrows (and ← / → while open) wrap around the set
next.addEventListener('click', () => show(state.index + 1));
prev.addEventListener('click', () => show(state.index - 1));
const show = (i) => {
  state.index = (i + state.items.length) % state.items.length;
  /* …re-clone the artwork + caption… */
};

MediaStablev1.1

Carousel

A transform-based slider engine with an owl-style API and zero dependencies: responsive `items`, `loop`, `nav` arrows, `dots`, `slideBy` (a count or "page"), `autoplay` with hover-pause, pointer `drag` with velocity snap, `lazyLoad` and a `margin` gutter. The track is translated with `transform`, never scrolled. Options arrive as `data-zak-carousel` JSON or through `new ZakUI.ZakCarousel(el, options)`.

Demo

Scroll-snap slides with arrows and dots.

01 · Design tokens
02 · Data grid
03 · AI surfaces
<div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel='{"items":2,"margin":12,"loop":true,"nav":true,"dots":true}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">…</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">…</div>
  </div>
</div>
<!-- Bare attribute = defaults: items 1, nav + dots + drag on, loop off -->
<div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">01 · Design tokens</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">02 · Data grid</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">03 · AI surfaces</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- Every option is JSON on the same attribute; the runtime generates the
     prev/next arrows and dots, so the markup only needs the track + slides -->
<div class="zak-carousel"
     data-zak-carousel='{"items":3,"margin":12,"loop":true,"autoplay":true,"autoplayTimeout":3000,"slideBy":"page"}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">
    <!-- slides… -->
  </div>
</div>
// Declarative — JSON on the attribute, auto-initialised on load and re-run after every playground render.
// <div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel='{"items":2,"slideBy":"page","dots":false}'>…</div>

// Imperative — the class is exposed on the global API.
const car = new ZakUI.ZakCarousel(el, {
  items: { 0: 1, 560: 2, 880: 3 },   // responsive: min container width → items
  loop: true,
  margin: 16,
  autoplay: true,
  autoplayTimeout: 4000,
  autoplayHoverPause: true,
  drag: true,
});

car.next();
car.prev();
car.to(2);        // jump to a stop index
car.destroy();    // detach observers + timers

// The engine reports movement through bubbling custom events.
el.addEventListener('zak:changed', (e) => console.log('stop', e.detail.index));
el.addEventListener('zak:translated', (e) => console.log('translated', e.detail.items, 'visible'));

Examples

One variant per card — the markup in each code tab is exactly what renders above it.

Multiple items

items shows several slides at once; margin is the pixel gutter and slideBy:"page" flips a whole view.

Alpha
Bravo

  <div class="zak-carousel__track">
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">Alpha</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">Bravo</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">Charlie</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">Delta</div>
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">Echo</div>
  </div>
</div>

Responsive items

items as an object maps a minimum container width to a count — the engine relayouts on resize.

Resize me
1 → 2 → 3
Mobile first
Desktop
Tablet
Wide
<!-- keys are min-width breakpoints (px), values are item counts -->
<div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel='{"items":{"0":1,"360":2,"640":3},"margin":12}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">…</div>
  </div>
</div>

Loop + autoplay

loop wraps last → first; autoplay advances on a timer and autoplayHoverPause holds it under the pointer.

Auto-advancing
Hover to pause
Loops forever
<div class="zak-carousel"
     data-zak-carousel='{"loop":true,"autoplay":true,"autoplayTimeout":2500,"autoplayHoverPause":true}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">…</div>
</div>

Drag / swipe

drag (on by default) lets a pointer pull the track; release snaps by distance or flick velocity.

Grab
Drag
Release
Snaps
<!-- drag is on by default; set "drag":false to disable pointer swiping -->
<div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel='{"items":2,"margin":10,"drag":true}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">…</div>
</div>

Lazy load

lazyLoad only assigns img[data-zak-src] when its slide scrolls into the visible set — here the cue is a placeholder label.

Loaded now
Loaded now
Loads on view
Loads on view
<div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel='{"items":2,"lazyLoad":true}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">
    <div class="zak-carousel__slide">
      <!-- src is withheld until the slide enters view, then moved from data-zak-src -->
      <img class="zak-img" data-zak-src="hero-04.webp" alt="Scene four"/>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

Arrows only (no dots)

dots:false drops the position dots; nav keeps the arrows. With one item, the engine clamps at the ends unless loop is on.

Step 1 of 3
Step 2 of 3
Step 3 of 3
<div class="zak-carousel" data-zak-carousel='{"dots":false,"nav":true}'>
  <div class="zak-carousel__track">…</div>
</div>

Usage

Slides are plain content — the engine only reads the track's direct children, so any markup works inside a .zak-carousel__slide.
loop wraps by jumping the index (no cloned items), so with items equal to the slide count it simply stays put.

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
data-zak-carouselattr{…}JSON options on the element; a bare attribute uses every default.
itemsnumber | {breakpoint: number}1Visible items — fixed, or keyed by minimum container width.
loopbooleanfalseWraps the last stop to the first (and back) instead of clamping.
navbooleantrueRenders prev/next arrows; false hides any authored arrows.
dotsbooleantrueRenders one position dot per reachable stop.
slideBynumber | "page"1Items to advance per step, or a whole view for "page".
autoplaybooleanfalseAuto-advances on a timer.
autoplayTimeoutnumber5000Milliseconds between auto-advances.
autoplayHoverPausebooleantruePauses autoplay while the pointer is over the carousel.
dragbooleantruePointer drag / swipe with distance- or velocity-based snap.
lazyLoadbooleanfalseAssigns img[data-zak-src] when its slide becomes visible.
marginnumber0Gutter between items, in pixels.
new ZakUI.ZakCarousel(el, opts)api—Imperative mount; instance exposes next(), prev(), to(i), destroy().
zak:changed / zak:translatedevent—Bubble from the root with { index, count, items } detail.
.zak-carousel__track / __slideelement—The engine translates the track and sizes each slide from items / margin.

A poster-first player: the gradient poster and play affordance keep the layout calm until intent — then the real <video> element takes over.

Demo

Video surface with poster overlay.

<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-video"
  data-zak-video
></div>
<!-- Poster-first 16:9 frame, near-black stage -->
<div class="zak-video" data-zak-video>
  <img class="zak-img" src="keynote-poster.webp" alt=""/>

  <!-- Full-frame trigger; radial scrim keeps the play glyph legible -->
  <button class="zak-video__overlay" type="button" data-video-overlay
          aria-label="Play video — Why teams choose ZAKUIKit, 2 minutes 47 seconds">
    <span class="zak-video__play">▶</span>
    <!-- Title + duration; drive the aria-label from it -->
    <span class="zak-video__meta">Why teams choose ZAKUIKit · 2:47</span>
  </button>
</div>
overlay.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const video = document.createElement('video');
  video.src = overlay.dataset.src;
  video.controls = true;
  video.autoplay = true;
  video.playsInline = true;
  overlay.replaceWith(video);      // swap poster for the real player
});

Usage

Always offer captions and a transcript link. Never autoplay with sound — the demo swaps in controls only after an explicit click.

// With a real source, mirror native events into the custom row
const el = document.createElement('audio');
el.src = '/episodes/24.mp3';

toggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
  const paused = el.paused;
  paused ? el.play() : el.pause();
  root.classList.toggle('is-playing', paused);
  toggle.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(paused));
});

el.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
  bar.style.setProperty('--value', (el.currentTime / el.duration) * 100 + '%');
});
