Data Visualization

Charts and dashboard primitives rendered as inline SVG.

8 components
Data VisualizationStablev1.0

Line Chart

The workhorse trend chart. The preview is an empty host — the runtime reads its `data-zak-chart` config and paints the SVG, grid, points and legend.

Demo

Trend lines with grid, points and tooltips.

<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div
  data-zak-chart
></div>
<!-- Minimal markup: one host, one config. The runtime mounts every [data-zak-chart] it finds -->
<div data-zak-chart='{"type":"line","data":{"labels":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"datasets":[{"label":"p95","data":[58,44,51]}]}}'></div>

<!-- The same config through the public API -->
<script>
  const chart = ZakChart.create('#latency', {
    // type: 'line' | 'area' | 'bar' | 'pie' | 'donut' | 'sparkline'
    type: 'line',
    data: {
      labels: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar'],
      datasets: [
        { label: 'p95 · this year', data: [58, 44, 51], color: 'var(--zak-chart-1)' },
        // A second dataset is drawn as the dashed comparison line
        { label: 'p95 · last year', data: [70, 66, 62], color: 'var(--zak-chart-2)' },
      ],
    },
    options: { width: 620, height: 240, grid: true, points: true, legend: true },
  });

  // Re-render with new data, or remove the chart from the host
  chart.update({ type: 'line', data: { datasets: [{ data: [30, 28, 24] }] } });
  chart.destroy();
</script>

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
type'line'—Chart family; the SVG is generated from the config.
data.labelsstring[]—X-axis ticks, distributed evenly across the plot.
data.datasets{ label, data, color }[]—Series list; index 0 is primary, index 1 is dashed.
options.pointsbooleantrueHoverable points with native <title> tooltips.
options.gridbooleantrueHorizontal grid lines and y-axis value labels.
options.legendbooleanautoLegend row built from the dataset labels.
options.width / heightnumber620 / 240SVG viewBox; the host scales it fluidly.

AI Prompt Input

The full composer: a growing textarea, context chips for attachments and tools, a send affordance that stays quiet until there is something to send, and keyboard hints that teach the shortcuts.

Demo

Auto-growing prompt composer with tools.

Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line 
<!-- Just declare this — the runtime generates the rest -->
<div class="zak-prompt"
  data-zak-prompt
></div>
<!-- Composer shell: focus-within paints the brand border and ring -->
<div class="zak-prompt" data-zak-prompt>
  <!-- Input: borderless auto-grow textarea, 3.4 to 9.5rem clamp -->
  <textarea class="zak-prompt__input" rows="2" placeholder="Describe the report you need…" aria-label="Prompt" data-zak-prompt-input></textarea>

  <div class="zak-prompt__bar">
    <div class="zak-prompt__chips">
      <!-- Chips: context chips for attach, model and tools; aria-pressed for toggles -->
      <button class="zak-prompt__chip" type="button" aria-label="Attach files">📎 Attach</button>
      <button class="zak-prompt__chip" type="button">🤖 zak-1-pro</button>
      <button class="zak-prompt__chip" type="button" aria-pressed="true">🌐 Web search</button>
    </div>

    <!-- Hint: teaches Enter and Shift+Enter once -->
    <span class="zak-prompt__hint">Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line</span>

    <!-- Send: gradient square pinned inline-end; disable at 40% while empty -->
    <button class="zak-prompt__send" type="button" aria-label="Send prompt" data-zak-prompt-send>➤</button>
  </div>
</div>
const prompt = document.querySelector('[data-zak-prompt]');
const input = prompt.querySelector('[data-zak-prompt-input]');
const send = prompt.querySelector('[data-zak-prompt-send]');

// Auto-grow the textarea between min (3.4rem) and max (9.5rem)
input.addEventListener('input', () => {
  input.style.height = 'auto';
  input.style.height = Math.min(input.scrollHeight, 152) + 'px';
});

// Dispatch a bubbling custom event — the host app owns the request
function submit() {
  const text = input.value.trim();
  if (!text) return;
  prompt.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('zak:prompt', {
    bubbles: true, detail: { text },
  }));
  input.value = '';
  input.style.height = 'auto';
}

send.addEventListener('click', submit);
input.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  if (e.key === 'Enter' && !e.shiftKey) { e.preventDefault(); submit(); }
});

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
.zak-promptclass—Composer shell; focus-within paints the brand border + ring.
.zak-prompt__inputelement—Borderless auto-grow textarea, 3.4–9.5rem clamp.
.zak-prompt__chipelement—Context chips: attach, model, tools. aria-pressed for toggles.
.zak-prompt__sendelement—Gradient square pinned inline-end; disable at 40% while empty.
.zak-prompt__hintelement—Teaches Enter / Shift+Enter once instead of on every use.

<!-- Outcome copy: phrase suggestions as results, verbs first -->
<textarea class="zak-prompt__input" id="suggest-prompt" rows="2" placeholder="Pick a suggestion above…" aria-label="Prompt"></textarea>
// Pills fill a prompt input and focus it — never auto-submit on click
suggest.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
  const pill = e.target.closest('.zak-suggest__pill');
  if (!pill) return;
  const input = document.querySelector(suggest.dataset.suggestTarget);
  input.value = pill.textContent.trim();
  input.focus();
  input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
});

outcome copypattern—Phrase suggestions as results ("Summarize…") — verbs first.

// Keep the newest message in view without fighting user scroll
const nearBottom = () =>
  thread.scrollHeight - thread.scrollTop - thread.clientHeight < 80;

new MutationObserver(() => {
  if (nearBottom()) thread.scrollTop = thread.scrollHeight;
}).observe(thread, { childList: true, subtree: true });

<!-- Done state: applied on the final token, the caret disappears -->

<!-- Busy state: true while typing, false when done, batches announcements -->
.zak-stream::after {
  content: "▍";
  display: inline-block;
  margin-inline-start: 1px;
  color: var(--zak-primary);
  animation: zak-blink 0.9s step-end infinite;
}

.zak-stream.is-done::after { display: none; }

@keyframes zak-blink { 50% { opacity: 0; } }
const stream = document.querySelector('[data-zak-stream]');
const bubble = document.querySelector('[data-zak-stream-bubble]');
const full = stream.dataset.streamText;
let i = 0, timer;

function type() {
  clearInterval(timer);
  i = 0;
  stream.classList.remove('is-done');
  bubble.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'true');

  timer = setInterval(() => {
    stream.textContent = full.slice(0, ++i);
    if (i >= full.length) {
      clearInterval(timer);
      stream.classList.add('is-done');        // drop the caret
      bubble.setAttribute('aria-busy', 'false');
    }
  }, 24);
}

replay.addEventListener('click', type);

Props API

PropertyTypeDefaultDescription
.zak-streamelement—Inline token sink; the ::after caret blinks via CSS.
.zak-stream.is-doneclass—Applied on the final token — the caret disappears.
aria-live="polite"attr—On the bubble; assistive tech reads newly arrived text.
aria-busyattr—True while typing, false when done — suppresses partial announces.

let step = 0;
const steps = [...panel.querySelectorAll('.zak-thinking__step')];

const advance = setInterval(() => {
  steps[step].classList.remove('is-current');
  steps[step].replaceChildren(checkIcon.cloneNode(true), steps[step].lastChild.textContent);
  step += 1;
  if (step >= steps.length) {
    clearInterval(advance);
    panel.classList.add('is-done');
    return;
  }
  steps[step].classList.add('is-current');
}, 1400);

Usage

Steps must reflect real work. Decorative step lists that always "complete" in order train users to ignore them.

Citation

Inline superscript chips wired to a numbered source list — the trust layer of AI prose. Chips lift to full brand on hover; sources stay one tap away.

Demo

Inline source references with footnote list.

Virtual grids hold a stable scroll position by writing tall spacer rows around the visible window1, while streaming responses must batch DOM writes to at most one per frame to avoid layout thrash2. Both techniques anchor on the same browser primitive: scroll anchoring3.

  • 1Virtual scrolling patterns — web.dev/articles/virtual-scrolling
  • 2Streaming UI without jank — developer.mozilla.org/…/Streams_API
  • 3CSS scroll anchoring — drafts.csswg.org/css-scroll-anchoring

// Filter as you type, keeping the highlight on a live option
input.addEventListener('input', () => {
  const q = input.value.toLowerCase();
  items.forEach((item) => {
    item.hidden = !item.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(q);
  });
  const first = items.find((i) => !i.hidden);
  items.forEach((i) => i.classList.toggle('is-active', i === first));
});

// Roving focus — arrows move, Enter activates
list.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
  const visible = [...items].filter((i) => !i.hidden);
  const current = visible.indexOf(document.activeElement);
  const next = e.key === 'ArrowDown' ? current + 1
             : e.key === 'ArrowUp'   ? current - 1 : -1;
  if (next >= 0) { e.preventDefault(); visible[next % visible.length].focus(); }
});
